source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Base the staffing mix primarily on staff seniority because competency differences are addressed after assignments are made.","B":"Use the same staffing pattern throughout the shift even when patient acuity and required competencies change.","C":"Base assignments primarily on staff scheduling preferences when the planned head count has been met.","D":"Base the staffing mix on patient care needs and acuity together with staff scope, education, skills, competencies, and relevant unit factors."}}
source_row.rationale: ANA staffing principles emphasize matching staffing resources to patient needs and considering patient acuity, skill mix, education, competencies, unit variables, and changing care demands. A fixed or seniority-only approach does not address safe staffing requirements.
source_row.source_detail: Staffing decisions incorporate patient needs, acuity, competencies, skill mix, and practice-setting factors Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.source_name: American Nurses Association — Principles for Nurse Staffing
source_row.stem: A charge nurse is determining the appropriate RN, LPN/LVN, and assistive-personnel mix for a shift. Which factors should drive the staffing decision?
